- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3-5 days), model often overshoots and overpredicts continuation; reduce forecast peak by 5-10% and add a slight downward slope.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.00 to +0.30), model frequently overestimates upward momentum; cap forecast growth to 1-2% above recent mean.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (especially 1st-5th days); add 0.5–1.5% to initial forecast values.  
- When sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from -0.5 to +0.3 in 3 days), model lags in adjusting; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead of sentiment shift to capture mean reversion.  
- Avoid forecasting below 60% of recent 18-day average unless sentiment is strongly bullish (>0.40) and volatility is high.
